chunks: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Walid al-Sulami told us, saying: Abu al-Fadl Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Katib al-Naysabouri told us, with a chain of narrators ascribed to the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), that he said:

The perfection of man is in six traits: with his two small things, his two big things, and his two guises. As for his two small things, they are his heart and tongue; if he fights, he fights with spirit (courage), and if he speaks, he speaks with a tongue. As for his two big things, they are his intellect and enthusiasm. As for his two guises, they are his wealth and beauty.
ai.seo_question: What are the six traits that define the perfection of a man according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes human perfection into the 'two small' (heart and tongue), 'two big' (intellect and ambition), and 'two guises' (wealth and beauty), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the integration of inner spiritual states with external social realities. This framework underscores that true *kamal* requires not only moral integrity and intellectual depth but also the proper management of one's material and physical presence in the world. It highlights the holistic nature of the ideal believer, where internal virtues manifest through external conduct and status.
